prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- There’s no one “best” site — pick the platform that matches the type of stay and the protections you want:
  - Airbnb: huge variety (rooms to entire homes), strong guest protections, rich reviews, filters like Superhost/Instant Book, higher service fees but good UX for long/unique stays.
  - Vrbo: focuses mostly on whole homes and family/group stays; fewer shared/room listings; good for vacations where you want an entire house.
  - Booking.com: strongest for hotels and professionally managed apartments, lots of instant-book options, flexible cancellation on many listings; sometimes cheaper because fees are less visible up front.

Which to choose by travel style
- Solo/short city trip or unique stays (treehouses, tiny homes): Airbnb.
- Family or group who need a whole house, multi-bedroom: Vrbo or Airbnb (compare both).
- When you want flexible, instant booking and hotel-level service or last-minute deals: Booking.com.
- If you prefer lower chance of dealing with an individual owner (more property managers/hotel-style): Booking.com or professionally managed VRBO/Airbnb listings.

How to find a good host — step-by-step checklist
1. Search smart
   - Filter for “entire place” if you want privacy; use dates, guest count, and must-have amenities (wifi, kitchen, parking, washer).
   - Sort by “review score” or “most reviews” to favor established listings.
   - Use the map to confirm location/neighborhood and distance to what you want.

2. Evaluate the listing and host profile
   - Read multiple recent reviews (last 6–12 months). Look for consistency on cleanliness, accuracy, communication, and check-in ease.
   - Check host status: Superhost/Top-Rated Host (Airbnb) or badges on Vrbo/Booking.com indicate reliable hosts.
   - Look for a completed profile with a photo and verified ID.
   - Prefer listings with many reviews across several months rather than a single batch of old reviews.

3. Look for operational details
   - Clear house rules, check-in/check-out instructions, and a detailed cancellation policy.
   - Accurate, high-quality photos and a complete amenities list.
   - Transparent total price (including cleaning and service fees). Compare final totals across platforms.

4. Communication test
   - Message the host before booking with a short question. Gauge response time and tone.
   - Responsive, polite, and helpful hosts are usually better during problems.

5. Check for red flags
   - Very few or no reviews for a listing that looks expensive.
   - Poor or inconsistent photos and vague descriptions.
   - Host asks to take the conversation or payment off-platform (never pay outside the platform).
   - Pressure to book immediately or offers to “discount if you contact me directly.”
   - Reviews that repeatedly mention safety, hidden fees, or misrepresented amenities.

6. Practical checks
   - Confirm Wi‑Fi speed if you need remote work (ask for a screenshot of a speed test).
   - Ask about parking specifics, access codes, elevators, noise, neighbors, and heating/AC.
   - Confirm the key/entry process, especially if arriving late.
   - Check if the host offers a flexible cancellation or refundable option if your dates may change.

Platform-specific tips
- Airbnb:
  - Look for Superhost and “Instant Book” if you want fast confirmation.
  - Check “House Rules,” “Guest access,” and the “Interaction with guests” sections.
  - Use the “Recent reviews” filter to see only the last year.
- Vrbo:
  - Good for whole-home listings and families. Look for long-stay discounts and bed counts per room.
  - Pay attention to damage deposit and cleaning fee policies.
- Booking.com:
  - Great for instant confirmations and many professionally managed properties.
  - Cancellation terms are often more flexible; check whether “Pay later” or “Free cancellation” applies.

Safety and payment
- Never pay outside the booking platform.
- Keep all communication on the platform (helps with dispute resolution).
- Consider travel insurance for expensive trips or non-refundable bookings.
- For extra security, choose listings with host ID verification and platforms’ built-in protections.

Sample short pre-booking message to a host
“Hi [Host name], I’m [first name] and I’ll be traveling with [number and relationship, e.g., two adults + one toddler]. We plan to arrive around [time] on [date]. Quick questions: is there safe parking on site? What’s the wifi speed (if I need to work)? Also, how do you handle check-in if we arrive late? Thanks — I look forward to hearing from you.”

What to do after booking
- Screenshot and save the booking confirmation and the host’s contact details.
- Reconfirm arrival time a few days before check-in.
- Review the house manual/check-in instructions and ask any last questions.
- If anything is wrong at check-in, message the host immediately and document issues with photos.

Quick summary recommendation
- If you want a unique local stay and protections: start with Airbnb.
- If you need a whole house for family/group stays: check Vrbo and Airbnb and compare totals.
- If you prefer hotels/professionally managed apartments and instant confirmation: use Booking.com.
- Use the checklist above to vet the host, and always keep communication and payment on-platform.

If you tell me your destination, travel dates, and travel style (solo, couple, family, business), I can give a tailored recommendation and a checklist of filters/phrases to use on each platform.
